question: Steady-state per-request cost of the ProcessReranker boundary versus the direct in-process scorer, and whether buffering the worker stdin changes it.
candidate_source: 9e792bc + BufWriter(64 KiB) around worker ChildStdin in src/reranking/process/transport.rs
workload: tests/fixtures/native-lifecycle-v1.json (4 synthetic cases x 20 candidates), batch_size 1, 20 candidates, threads 2, MiniLMv2 verified snapshot, ONNX Runtime 1.32.0
design: Both scorers loaded once in one parent; per round the same case is scored by both in ABBA order (even rounds direct first). Score bits must match each round. Blocks alternate base, cand, base, cand; 240 rounds per block. All rounds are kept; no warmup removal except the separately labelled smoke run, which is not counted.
primary_metrics: per-case p95 worker/direct total ratio per block (declared gate <= 1.10)
median and p95 of paired per-round difference worker - direct (ms)
candidate versus baseline difference of the paired median overhead
claims_policy: No improvement is claimed unless the candidate paired-overhead median is lower than the baseline in both block pairs; any regression is retained.
conditions: Same host (M5 Max, 64 GiB), no other compute-intensive task running; not a cold-load or lifecycle measurement.
